notes: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 reached GA on 2026-08-13 under the deepseek-v4-pro API model ID; this profile retains the model's documented capability metadata for provenance.

Beginning 2026-09-14T04:00:00Z, DeepSeek routes all requests made with the deepseek-v4-pro model ID to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and bills them at V4.1-Flash rates until V4.1 Pro launches. DeepSeek states that V4 Pro is being phased out in an orderly manner.
CKB therefore marks deepseek-v4-pro as deprecated rather than retired: the slug remains accepted by the provider, but new work should select deepseek-flash explicitly.

DeepSeek's current model table continues to mark Vision as unsupported for the deepseek-v4-pro entry, so this profile remains text-input-only and does not infer image support from the backend routing behavior.
DeepSeek's official Codex integration declares a 1,048,576-token context window for deepseek-v4-pro, and the API reference allows a maximum output of 393,216 tokens (384K).
Thinking and non-thinking modes are supported. reasoning_effort supports low, high, and max; high is the documented default. minimal maps to low, while medium and xhigh map to high for compatibility.

In thinking mode, temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty are accepted for compatibility but have no effect. top_p is effective with a lower bound of 0.95; in non-thinking mode top_p is fixed at 1.0.
JSON object output and JSON-schema structured output are supported.

Function calling is supported, and DeepSeek's official Codex model catalog declares supports_parallel_tool_calls=true. On the Responses API the parallel_tool_calls request parameter itself is ignored because parallel tool calling is always enabled.

The Responses API supports the apply_patch custom tool. Its current compatibility table marks web_search, file_search, code_interpreter, computer_use, MCP, and other built-in tool types as ignored; CKB therefore does not advertise those as generally supported tools for this profile.

DeepSeek's Anthropic/Claude integration separately documents provider-side web search behavior, so web-search availability is API-surface-specific and is not promoted to a global named-tool capability in this profile.
No knowledge cutoff is declared in the checked primary documentation.
